title: The Cheese Castle Kingdom
seo_title: Cheese Castle Charcuterie Board: How It's Built & What to Buy
description: A cheese castle charcuterie board for 12 to 15: walls of cheddar bricks, salami chub towers with prosciutto roofs and a brie courtyard. The hardest board in the book.
hook: A fortress of cheese bricks with salami towers, prosciutto roofs and a brie courtyard.
why: The walls are cheese bricks set with cream cheese mortar on a hidden box, so they stand up straight instead of sliding. Four whole salami chubs make the towers, topped with prosciutto roofs.

Inside the walls, a brie courtyard, and around them cubes of Gouda, salami and fruit feed the guests. It's rated 5 of 5, the hardest board in the book and the most fun, and it's the one people will photograph.

timeline.what: Cut all the cheese bricks and build the castle walls (keep it wrapped in the fridge). Shape the prosciutto roofs.
Set the castle on the board, add the towers and the drawbridge.
Lay the moat, then the kingdom around it.
Add the rosemary flags and the forest.

faq.q: How do you make a cheese castle?
faq.a: Stack cheddar bricks with cream cheese mortar around a hidden box so the walls stand straight, then add whole salami chubs as towers. The book has the step-by-step build.
About 2½ hours of active time. It's the most complex board in the book.

Cut the cheese bricks the day before and keep them wrapped. Build the castle on the day. Keep meat, cheese and cut fruit out no more than 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F. For a long party, build half, keep the refill in the fridge and top it up halfway through.
